summary.text: The Puerto Rico Trench runs north of Puerto Rico on the boundary between the North Atlantic and the Caribbean Sea, and holds the Atlantic's deepest points.
It lies where two plates slide past each other along a transform boundary, with only a small amount of subduction.
It has produced earthquakes above magnitude 8.0, and studies conclude a quake along it could set off a significant tsunami.

facts.label: Victor Vescovo's dive
facts.value: Reached the deepest point on 19 December 2018

items.prompt: The subduction zone at the Puerto Rico Trench has not ruptured in over 200 years. Why does that worry geophysicists?

options.label: It means the zone is shrinking away
They think a major event may be due
It means their instruments have failed
It shows the trench is filling with mud

items.explain: Geophysicists believe the long quiet spell may mean the subduction zone is due for a major event.

items.prompt: At the Puerto Rico Trench, what are the two plates mostly doing?

options.label: Pulling apart to make new seafloor
Colliding head-on and piling up
Sliding past one another sideways
Sitting still with no movement

items.explain: The plates pass each other along a transform boundary with only a small component of subduction.

items.prompt: Volcanoes erupt often in the Lesser Antilles southeast of Puerto Rico, yet Puerto Rico has had no active volcanoes for about 30 million years. What explains the difference?

options.label: A plate dives more directly to the southeast
Puerto Rico's crust is too thick to erupt
The deep trench cools the rock below Puerto Rico
The Lesser Antilles sit on a mantle hot spot

items.explain: At the trench subduction is oblique, while to the southeast the South American plate is subducted more directly along the Lesser Antilles zone, which explains the active volcanoes.

items.prompt: After the 2004 tsunami struck more than 40 countries around the Indian Ocean, how did the Caribbean respond?

options.label: Islanders largely ignored the risk
Coastal towns were moved inland
Building on beaches was banned
Local governments began emergency planning

items.explain: Many more people came to fear such an event in the Caribbean, and local governments began emergency planning.

items.prompt: The Puerto Rico Trench holds which depth record?

options.label: The deepest point on Earth
The deepest points in the Atlantic
The longest trench in the world
The deepest point near the equator

items.explain: The trench constitutes the deepest points in the Atlantic Ocean, reaching between 8,376 and 8,740 m.

items.prompt: North of Puerto Rico, about how fast does the North American plate move relative to the Caribbean plate?

options.label: About 20 mm a year
About 20 cm a year
About 20 m a year
About 2 km a year

items.explain: At the site of the 2014 earthquake the North America plate moves at roughly 20 mm per year relative to the Caribbean plate.
